about: A retelling of Zork II: the Wizard of Frobozz. You start in a barrow, cross a cavern and bridge, meet a wand-waving Wizard, and pass a Carousel Room and a topiary garden with a gazebo and a unicorn.

done.why: I got to a pretty garden and a newspaper joke in about 17 turns. I had no goal and nothing pulled me on, and I'm impatient. The unicorn's key wasn't takeable, which stalled my one lead. I quit.

moments.note: The Wizard appears, waves his wand and vanishes. The sword flickers glowing and not glowing.
The Carousel Room scrambles directions, so I had no idea where I was going.
The hedge creatures in the topiary garden are shown with some wit, as the dragon examine text shows.
The unicorn and its key are described, but 'take key' answers 'can't see any such thing'.

wished: A clearer sense of what I'm trying to do
To take or interact with the unicorn's key

lines.line: A moment ago it was looking at you, or you thought so.
lines.why: The dragon hedge was the best, creepiest bit of writing I read.

lines.line: The Wizard, in a deep and resonant voice, speaks the word "Fantasize!" He then vanishes, cackling gleefully.
lines.why: An early hook that promised the Wizard as a character.

fun.why: Some charm, but no hook and no direction in a few minutes.

engagement.why: There was nothing to chase, so I quit.

difficulty.why: It felt aimless rather than hard, and the unicorn's key was awkward.

interestingness.why: The setting is familiar from Zork and has some good touches.

prose.why: The prose is evocative, especially the garden and the dragon.
